body:
[Jadon Jones vs Koby Brea](https://barttorvik.com/playerstat.php?link=y&sIndex=6&minusage=16.5&minDR=13&minAst=9&mintp100=10&minht=77&cvalue=SEC&year=career&start=20251101&end=20260501&usageSelect=-1&drebSelect=-1&astSelect=-1)

Statistically, they're identical in weak passing+rebounding volume, low usage, and high 3PT volume. Jadon's strengths show he's a more functional athlete (triple the free throw rate, blk%, and stl% Brea posted, as well as a higher rim frequency, meaning he can maneuver past defenders).

The only strength Brea carried was a higher 3PT%. The difference between Jones' 37% and Brea's 43% is significant, but season-by-season 3PT% is a high-variance metric and can fail to have an effect on team efficiency. In Brea's rookie season, he shot 34.8% from 3 in the G and had the worst ORTG on-off swing of Valley Suns rotation players last season. 

Jones provides more stable game-by-game impact on the wing than Brea, regardless of points per game or name value.

author: nilehoops
body:
70 win% over his last 91 games. 60 true shooting/16 OREB%/29 DREB%/9 AST%/5 BLK% across those games. 

No NBA player has ever done this across a single season. Decreasing the parameters to 56 TS%/12 OREB%/24 DREB%/8 AST%/5 BLK% on 18+ usage, and only David Robinson, Robert Parish, Dwight Howard, and Shaq have done it. 

His pro dominance is no coincidence, referring to his NCAA priors. 6 players have career numbers of ≥60 True Shooting; ≥13 OREB%; ≥22 DREB%; ≥8 AST%; ≥0.5 A:TO; 5.25 BLK%: Ayton, Edey, Clingan, KAT, Aleks Maric, and **Josh Ibarra**.

[Def Reb % ≥ 15.5; Steal % ≥ 2.75; 3PA/100 Poss ≥ 6; Height ≥ 80; Minutes ≥ 1000;](https://barttorvik.com/playerstat.php?link=y&sIndex=35&minDR=15.5&minStl=2.75&mintp100=6&minht=80&minmpg=1000&year=career&minmin=0&start=20251101&end=20260501)

8 players in Bart have exhibited this level of rebounding, stealing, and 3-point volume at 6'8+; **Terri Miller Jr. and Kasean Pryor** are two of them. 

Pending Pryor's signing with MEX, the only other pair of teammates are **Paul George and Robert Covington**, who collaborated on the Clippers [for a +12.7 net rating vs. a +0.9 team baseline over the three-season sample they were both on the roster.](https://databallr.com/wowy/LAC/2022/2024/all/all/wowy/202331/203496)

We can mimic this two-way lineup floor by pairing the two.
